title: Marketing research
summary: Sourced marketing briefs: competitor traffic and channels, messaging history, rising search demand, and creator and podcast partners.
when: competitors' traffic or channels, how a site's messaging or pricing changed, content ideas from search demand, or creators, podcasts and sponsorships to partner with
askFirst: Their brand or site, the competitors (domains) and the market or country.
The target audience and the goal: a campaign, content plan, partner shortlist or launch readout.
The time window, and how many credits they are willing to spend.

recipes.title: Know where competitors win
recipes.when: Comparing competitors' traffic, acquisition channels and positioning.

steps.do: Traffic, engagement and marketing channel shares per domain for one complete month.
Find a homepage capture per year with history, then read its text with content.
Disambiguate brand terms, then find related and rising queries.

recipes.output: Traffic and channel mix, how each story changed, and three campaign opportunities, with every figure cited.

recipes.title: Catch demand before everyone else
recipes.when: Content ideas from growing search interest.

steps.do: Find topics with growing interest and their rising queries.
See which pages already rank for the best queries and read the top results.

recipes.output: Rising queries, who already ranks, and three article briefs with audience and sources.

recipes.title: Find your next audience
recipes.when: Shortlisting podcasts and creators to sponsor or partner with.

steps.do: Find relevant shows and the sponsors already buying them.
Find creators by handle, name or bio, with follower counts.

recipes.output: A five-partner shortlist with audience, topic and sponsor evidence, and caveats.

recipes.title: Messaging and pricing history
recipes.when: How a homepage, pricing page or launch page changed over time.

steps.do: Pick captures by date (history with date) and read each version's text.
Optionally check whether traffic or search interest moved after each change.

recipes.output: A dated change log of headline, plans and prices, with what each change signals.

rules: Check each capability's current inputs and price with firecrawl_find_tools before calling it, and tell the user the cost before a paid call. Similarweb bills per returned metric or row and costs far more than the other sources, so confirm first and keep metrics and limits small.
When a provider needs its data terms accepted, show the terms and ask an organization admin to accept them in the Firecrawl dashboard. A data request is never acceptance.

Every figure names its source. Label Similarweb figures as estimates. Oriane and Particle search indexes, so an empty result means not indexed, not absent. Say what is missing or failed; never invent metrics.
Return a short brief: findings, sources, and actionable next steps.
